CHIEF COMPLAINT
Lung nodule found on imaging.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient presents with a three-month history of cough that began after loading hay with horses. Initially thought to have developed a cold, which prompted a visit to PCP. PCP diagnosed bronchitis and ordered chest X-ray to rule out pneumonia. Chest X-ray revealed a lung nodule, which was confirmed on subsequent CT scan. Patient reports cough has since resolved. Denies current pain or shortness of breath.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies pain, shortness of breath, or fever. Cough has resolved.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis, fairly controlled. Previous smoker, quit approximately seven years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 7.5 mg weekly for rheumatoid arthritis.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother with history of breast cancer, currently doing well. No family history of lung cancer or other malignancies. No previous history of lung infections or pneumonia in patient.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient exercises regularly, bikes frequently on trails. Previously smoked but quit seven years ago. Has horses.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: BP 124/76, HR 70, RR 16, O2 sat 98% on room air, afebrile. Lungs clear and equal bilaterally. Heart regular rate and rhythm without clicks, rubs, murmurs, or extra beats. Extremities: skin pink, warm, and dry without edema. Mild swelling noted at knuckles of third digits bilaterally consistent with rheumatoid arthritis. Pulses intact in all extremities with brisk capillary refill.

RESULTS
Chest CT shows solitary 2 cm nodule in lateral aspect of right upper lobe with smooth appearance. No evidence of emphysematous disease.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Incidentally found right upper lobe lung nodule. Plan to order pulmonary function tests for baseline lung function assessment. PET CT to be scheduled to determine if nodule is metabolically active. Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery recommended for nodule removal with small portion of lung; procedure under general anesthesia lasting approximately 1.5 hours. Patient will require hospitalization for one night with chest tube placement, to be removed at bedside the following day. For rheumatoid arthritis, continue current follow-up with rheumatologist and continue methotrexate therapy as previously outlined.
